judges.verdict: All 19 builds pass build, vet, gofmt and their own tests, including under -race. Every one meets the core spec: strong ETag on GET/HEAD 200s, a handler-set ETag is kept, weak, list and * matching give 304, and other methods and non-200 statuses pass through. What separates them is fidelity at the edges and proportionality. A, J and M are compact, correct and stream on Flush, with A's lenient parser and small test suite the cleanest. The heaviest builds (D, E, F) add meta-tests, coupling to Compress's private type, or Content-Length emulation, which buys nothing for users. G ranks last because it buffers even non-200 responses, ignores Flush on them, loses trailers, and drops buffered output on Hijack.
